title: Nonzero ideal sheaf iff its generic stalk is nontrivial and surjective
statement: Let (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] and (J : X.IdealSheafData). Then (J ≠ ⊥ ↔ Nontrivial ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (genericPoint X)).obj J.toModules)) ∧ (J ≠ ⊥ ↔ Function.Surjective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (genericPoint X)).map J.toModulesι).hom).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YL

proof.text: On an affine neighborhood of the generic point the affine zero-set theorem gives surjectivity iff the section ideal is not bottom, since the generic point is the zero prime. Use the proved affine-section criterion and ideal_bot to obtain the surjectivity equivalence.

Lift a nonzero affine ideal element to an ideal-module section. Its generic germ cannot vanish: equality of its image germ with zero would force its restriction to a smaller nonempty open to vanish, contradicting map_injective_of_isIntegral. Conversely, when J is bottom, represent any germ and shrink to an affine neighborhood; range_toModulesι_app and ideal_bot force the image to vanish, and sectionwise injectivity forces the representative to vanish. Thus every germ is zero.

    (J : X.IdealSheafData) :
    (J ≠ ⊥ ↔
        Nontrivial ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (genericPoint X)).obj
          J.toModules)) ∧
      (J ≠ ⊥ ↔
        Function.Surjective
          ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (genericPoint X)).map
            J.toModulesι).hom)
